methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $30M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 4 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $2.0B.

data.narrative:
Shinkei, a Series A robotics and manufacturing company founded by Saif Khawaja and Reed Ginsberg, has raised $30M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comparable universe of 9 private firms and 1 public company (277810.KQ) in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including peers at seed through Series B stages: Generalist AI ($2.0B Series B), Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B Seed).

Two triangulation methods apply. Stage-progression analysis uses the $30M raised as a proxy base value and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression, implying $60M. Peer-median methodology leverages the four comparable transactions noted above, yielding a median valuation of $1.7B with a range of $1.1B to $2.0B.

The two methods produce a wide implied range: $51M (low end from stage-progression) to $2.0B (high end from peer median). The median triangulated value across both approaches is $880M. This disparity reflects the stage gap between Shinkei (Series A) and most peers (Series B), as well as company-specific execution risk. Key uncertainties center on technology differentiation, path to Series B, and how Shinkei's specific capabilities and traction compare to the median peer profile. The peer set suggests substantial capital availability in the sector, but valuation compression risk exists if market conditions tighten.
